newsitem.title: UK: UK's Norwich Union details 1997 bonus rates.
newsitem.headline: UK's Norwich Union details 1997 bonus rates.

text.p: UK insurance and investment group Norwich Union, which plans to go public this year, on Wednesday gave details of the 1997 bonuses for its life and pensions policy customers.
"With profits policies continue to perform well with real returns of the order of 4.5 percent per annum above inflation," said Richard Harvey, Norwich Union's group finance director.
Norwich Union said in a statement that annual bonus rates for its unitised business remain unchanged in 1997, with rates of 6.5 percent for savings and 7.5 percent for pensions.
Annual bonus rates on conventional with-profits life business were maintained at 2.5 percent on guaranteed benefit and 4.5 percent on attaching bonuses.

For its pensions business, Norwich Union said the bonus on guaranteed benefit was maintained at 2.5 percent but the rate on attaching bonuses was lower at 4.5 percent compared with 5.5 percent for 1996.
"Equities made good progress in 1996 and fixed interest markets produced returns well above inflation. Property also performed reasonably well," Harvey said.

"The outlook for inflation remains encouragingly low, confirming our view that while real investment returns will remain good, low inflation will mean that overall returns will be more subdued in the 1990s," he added.
